questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of Asha and Lata is 5 : 6. If the difference between their ages is 6 years, then what will be Lata’s age after 5 years?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the present ages of Asha and Lata is 5 : 6. If the difference between their ages is 6 years, then what will be Lata’s age after 5 years?
questions.solution:
According to the given information,

The ratio of present ages of Asha and Lata = 5 : 6

Let the ages of Asha and Lata be 5x and 6x respectively. 

Difference between their ages is 6 years

6x – 5x = 6

x = 6

Then,

Asha’s age, 5x = 5 × 6 = 30

Lata’s age, 6x = 6 × 6 = 36

Lata’s age after 5 years = 36 + 5 = 41

Lata’s age after 5 years is ‘41’

Hence, “41” is the correct answer.

questions.question: The cost of an apple is four less than twice the cost of a banana, and that of a papaya is half the cost of an apple. If the total cost of the fruits is Rs. 150, then what is the cost of a banana?
questions.questionHtml: The cost of an apple is four less than twice the cost of a banana, and that of a papaya is half the cost of an apple. If the total cost of the fruits is Rs. 150, then what is the cost of a banana?
questions.solution:
Given,

Cost of banana = x

The cost of an apple is four less than twice the cost of a banana.

Cost of apple = 2x - 4

Papaya is half the cost of an apple.

Cost of papaya = (2x - 4) / 2

Total cost of fruits = 150/-

∴ Cost of banana + apple + papaya = 150/-

⇒ x + (2x - 4) + (2x - 4) / 2 = 150

⇒ 2x + 4x - 8 + 2x - 4 = 300

⇒ 8x - 12 = 300

⇒ 8x = 312

⇒ x = 312 / 8

⇒ x = 39

∴ Here, the cost of banana = x.

So, the cost of banana = 39/-

Hence, the correct answer is "Rs. 39".

questions.question: Which one of the following statements regarding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) is not correct?
questions.questionHtml: Which one of the following statements regarding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) is not correct?

options.html: An OCI is a citizen of another country.

options.text: An OCI possesses multiple-entry long-term visa for visiting India.
options.html: An OCI possesses multiple-entry long-term visa for visiting India.

options.text: An OCI is at par with NRIs in all matters
options.html: An OCI is at par with NRIs in all matters

options.text: An OCI is not entitled to the fundamental right to equality of opportunity in public employment.
options.html: An OCI is not entitled to the fundamental right to equality of opportunity in public employment.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is An OCI is at par with NRIs in all matters.

  • Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) refers all the Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs) who were citizens of India on 26th January 1950 or thereafter or were eligible to become citizens of India on 26th January 1950 except who is or had been a citizen of Pakistan, Bangladesh or such other country as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify.
  • A registered Overseas Citizen of India enjoys the following benefits:
    • he/she is granted multiple entries, multi-purpose, life-long visa for visiting India,
    • he/she is exempted from registration with Foreign Regional Registration Officer or Foreign Registration Officer for any length of stay in India, and
    • is entitled to general 'parity with Non-Resident Indians in respect of all facilities available to them in economic, financial and educational fields except in matters relating to the acquisition of agricultural or plantation properties'.
    • However, OCI is not at par with NRIs in all the matters.

 

  • NRI means Non-Resident Indian. NRI is a residential status given to a citizen of India with an Indian Passport who resides in a foreign country for the purpose of work/business, or education.
  • The eligibility criteria for NRI status is that the person should be an Indian citizen with a valid Indian Passport and should reside outside of India for at least 183 days or more in a financial year (April 1st – March 31st).
  • Until the year 2010, NRIs were not allowed to vote in the elections.
  • However, post-2010 an amendment permitted NRIs to vote at their particular constituency in India but the voting required the direct presence of the NRI in India at the particular polling booth where the name was registered.

Consider the following statements about the Morley Minto reforms of 1909:

The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

Key Points

  • Indian Councils Act 1909 / Morley-Minto reforms:- 
    • The Indian Councils Act 1909 was an act of the British Parliament that introduced a few reforms in the legislative councils and increased the involvement of Indians (limited) in the governance of British India.
    • It was more commonly called the Morley-Minto Reforms after the Secretary of State for India John Morley and the Viceroy of India, Minto.
    • It provided for limited self-government by increasing the number of elected Indians in the Legislative Councils. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
    • It retained an official majority in the Central Legislative Council but allowed the provincial legislative councils to have a non-official majority.
    • It introduced a system of communal representation for Muslims by accepting the concept of a ‘separate electorate’.
    • Under this, the Muslim members were to be elected only by Muslim voters
    • The Act did nothing to grant colonial self-government, which was Congress’s demand.
  • The timespan of acts:-
    • Indian Councils Act of 1861 – 31 years
    • Indian Councils Act of 1892 – 17 years
    • Indian Councils Act of 1909 – 10 years. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
    • Government of India Act 1919 – 16 years

questions.question: Who was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to start military expeditions into southern India?
questions.questionHtml: Who was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to start military expeditions into southern India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Alauddin Khalji.

Key Points

  • Alauddin Khalji was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to start military expeditions into southern India.
  • Alauddin Khalji ​:
    • He was the nephew and son-in-law of Jalaluddin Khilji, who laid the foundation of the Khilji dynasty in 1290.
    • He was named Amir-i-Tuzuk because he had supported his uncle in his quest for dominance.
    • Alauddin led two successful expeditions during Jalaluddin's rule.
    • In addition to the Iqta of Kara, Bhilsa (Vidisa) was granted the Iqta of Awadh during his first expedition in AD 1292.
    • In addition, he was named Arizi-i-Mumalik, or Minister of War. He oversaw the first Turkish expedition to southern India in AD 1294, during which they pillaged Devagiri.
    • The expedition's triumph demonstrated Alauddin's skill as a military leader and effective organizer.
    • He slew Jalaluddin Khilji in July of the year 1296 and appointed himself as the Sultan.
    • Alauddin made the decision to bring back Balban's brutal political practices.
    • He made the decision to limit the nobility's authority and the ulema's (Islamic scholars') meddling in domestic affairs.
    • In the early years of his reign, he also had to deal with a few secessions, one after another.

Additional Information

  • Ghiyas-ud-din Balban was one of the most potent sultans of the Middle Ages, he was the Sultan of Delhi from 1266 until 1287 AD.
    • Like his mentor, Iltutmish, he ascended to prominence and assumed the title of Sultan of Delhi.
    • Balban belonged to the renowned Iltutmish's group of 40 Turkish slaves.
    • He brought peace and order back to the realm, together with the authority and dignity of the sultan, after thirty years of near-anarchy since the days of Iltutmish.
    • Balban also forced officials to respect the Sultan. They needed to touch his feet and bow. It was known as Sijda.
    • He created a spy system to watch over officials who were called Barids.
    • He also introduced the Iqta system, which granted land to officials in exchange for their services.
    • He made reforms to the police system. He created a separate police force called the Kotwali, which had the authority to enforce the law and punish offenders.
  • Muhammad bin Tughluq (MBT) was the son of Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq, also known as Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, who founded the Tughlaq dynasty by subduing the Delhi Sultanate. 
    • Other names for him are Ulugh Khan and Prince Fakhr Malik Jauna Khan.
    • The Deccan region of India, which is now Maharashtra, is home to Daulatabad, also called Devagiri, and it was Tughluq who ordered the relocation of his capital from Delhi.
    • He introduced token money in the form of brass and copper coins with a par value with gold and silver coins.
  • Iltutmish was the first Muslim ruler to rule from Delhi and that's why he was regarded as the effective founder of the Delhi Sultanate.
    • He was also the first Sultan of India to be recognised by the Khalifa.
    • He was successful in protecting Delhi's throne from the Mongol invasion as well as Yeldoz and Qubacha attacks.
    • He shattered the Rajput powers in the north and established his dominance over them.
    • He made his rule hereditary, issued coins in his honour, and made Delhi a beautiful capital.
    • He completed the construction of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and the Qutb Minar.
    • He unveiled the Sultanate's two coinage, the copper jital and the silver tanka.
    • He introduced the Iqtadari system, which divided the country into Iqtas and allocated them to nobles in return for pay.
    • Since he did not think his sons were capable of carrying out the role, he passed away in 1236 and was succeeded by his daughter, Razia Sultana.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a bacterial disease?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is not a bacterial disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Asthma.

  • Asthma is not a bacterial disease.
  • Asthma is a condition in which your airways narrow and swell and may produce extra mucus.
  • Asthma can make breathing difficult and trigger coughing, a whistling sound (wheezing) when you breathe out, and shortness of breath.

Key Points

  • Asthma signs and symptoms are:
    • Shortness of breath.
    • Chest tightness or pain.
    • Wheezing when exhaling, which is a common sign of asthma in children.
    • Trouble sleeping caused by shortness of breath, coughing or wheezing.
    • Coughing or wheezing attacks are worsened by a respiratory virus, such as a cold or the flu.
  • Types of Asthma are:
    • Allergic asthma: Allergens trigger this common type of asthma.
    • Nonallergic asthma: Irritants in the air not related to allergies trigger this type of asthma.
    • Occupational asthma:  Occupational asthma is a type of asthma induced by triggers in the workplace.

Additional Information

Disease Details
Typhoid

Typhoid is a bacterial infection that can lead to a high fever, diarrhoea, and vomiting.

It can be fatal. It is caused by the bacteria Salmonella typhi.

The infection is often passed on through contaminated food and drinking water, and it is more prevalent in places where handwashing is less frequent.
Plague

Plague is an infectious disease caused by Yersinia pestis bacteria, usually found in small mammals and their fleas.

The disease is transmitted between animals via their fleas and, as it is a zoonotic bacterium, it can also transmit from animals to humans
Diphtheria

Diphtheria is a serious infection caused by strains of bacteria called Corynebacterium diphtheriae that make toxins (poison).

It can lead to difficulty in breathing, heart failure, paralysis, and even death.

CDC recommends vaccines for infants, children, teens, and adults to prevent diphtheria.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: 'D) Aihole.'

Key Points

    • It was a prominent center of art, culture, and architecture during their reign.
    • Aihole is often referred to as the "Cradle of Indian Temple Architecture" due to its numerous rock-cut temples and structural monuments built by the Chalukyas.
    • The Chalukyas later shifted their capital to Badami (Vatapi), but Aihole remained a significant cultural hub.

Incorrect Statements

  • Bharuch:
    • Bharuch, an ancient port city in Gujarat, was not associated with the Chalukyas but was significant for maritime trade during various periods.

Hence, the correct option is: D) Aihole.

Additional Information

  • Chalukya Dynasty:
    • The Chalukyas were known for their contributions to Indian art and architecture, particularly in the Deccan region.
    • Their architectural achievements include the rock-cut temples at Badami, the structural temples at Aihole, and the famous Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal (a UNESCO World Heritage Site).
  • Significance of Aihole:
    • Aihole houses over 100 temples, showcasing various architectural styles, from early rock-cut caves to later structural temples.
    • The Durga Temple and Lad Khan Temple are notable examples of Chalukyan architecture in Aihole.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 6,400 invested on the basis of yearly compounding of interest, grows to Rs. 7,056 in two years. What is the percentage rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 6,400 invested on the basis of yearly compounding of interest, grows to Rs. 7,056 in two years. What is the percentage rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For Compound Interest over 2 years, Rate% = [√(Amount ÷ Principal) − 1] × 100

⇒ Rate% = [√(7056 ÷ 6400) − 1] × 100

⇒ Rate% = (84/80 − 1) × 100

⇒ Rate% = (21/20 − 1) × 100 = (1/20) × 100 = 5%

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = Rs. 6400

Amount (A) = Rs. 7056

Time (t) = 2 years

Formula Used:

A = P(1 + R/100)t

Calculation:

⇒ 7056 = 6400(1 + R/100)2

⇒ (1 + R/100)2 = 7056 ÷ 6400

⇒ (1 + R/100)2 = 441 ÷ 400

⇒ (1 + R/100)2 = (21 ÷ 20)2

Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ 1 + R/100 = 21/20

⇒ R/100 = 21/20 − 1

⇒ R/100 = 1/20

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 20 = 5%

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Additional Information

Effective Rate for 2 Years

The effective compound interest rate for 2 years at R% per annum can be calculated using successive percentage change: Effective CI% = R + R + (R × R)/100.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

For the first year, SI and CI are equal on a certain sum. The difference arises from the second year because CI includes interest earned on the accumulated interest. Difference for 2 years = P(R/100)2.

Multiplying Factor Method

In CI, the multiplying factor for one year is (1 + R/100). If compounded for t years, the total growth factor becomes (1 + R/100)t. To find the rate, you simply take the t-th root of the ratio Amount ÷ Principal.

questions.question: Find the interest earned in the first year on ₹ 200 at 20% p.a. compound interest, interest compounded every three months.
questions.questionHtml: Find the interest earned in the first year on ₹ 200 at 20% p.a. compound interest, interest compounded every three months.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Quarterly Rate = 20% ÷ 4 = 5% and cycles = 4.

Effective rate for 4 cycles of 5% is calculated by combining 5% successively:

For 2 cycles: 5 + 5 + (5 × 5)/100 = 10.25%

For 4 cycles: 10.25 + 10.25 + (10.25 × 10.25)/100 = 20.5 + 1.050625 = 21.550625%

Interest = 21.550625% of ₹ 200 = 21.550625 × 2 = ₹ 43.10125

∴ The correct answer is ₹ 43.101.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹ 200

Annual Rate (R) = 20%

Time (T) = 1 year

Interest is compounded every 3 months (quarterly).

Formula Used:

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)n

Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

Where r is the rate per compounding period and n is the number of periods.

Calculations:

⇒ Quarterly Rate (r) = 20% ÷ 4 = 5% per quarter

⇒ Number of cycles (n) = 1 year × 4 = 4 quarters

⇒ Amount (A) = 200 × (1 + 5/100)4

⇒ Amount (A) = 200 × (1.05)4

⇒ Amount (A) = 200 × 1.21550625 = 243.10125

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = 243.10125 − 200 = 43.10125

⇒ Rounding off to three decimal places, CI = 43.101

∴ The correct answer is ₹ 43.101.

Additional Information

Quarterly Compounding

When interest is compounded quarterly, the annual rate R is divided by 4 (R/4), and the time T in years is multiplied by 4 (4T) to get the number of periods.

Half-Yearly Compounding

When compounded half-yearly, the rate becomes R/2 and the time periods become 2T.

Effective Rate for Two Cycles

The effective compound interest rate for two equal cycles at R% can be found directly using the successive percentage formula: 2R + R2/100.

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated purely on the principal amount, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the principal along with previously accumulated interest.

questions.question: A merchant has 1000kg of sugar, part of which he sells at 8% profit and the rest at 18% profit. He gains 14% on the whole. The quantity sold at 18% profit is:
questions.questionHtml: A merchant has 1000kg of sugar, part of which he sells at 8% profit and the rest at 18% profit. He gains 14% on the whole. The quantity sold at 18% profit is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of quantities sold = (18 − 14) : (14 − 8)

Ratio = 4 : 6 = 2 : 3

Total units = 2 + 3 = 5 units → 1000 kg

1 unit = 200 kg

Quantity sold at 18% profit (3 units) = 3 × 200 = 600 kg

∴ The correct option is B.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Sugar = 1000 kg

Profit on Part 1 = 8%

Profit on Part 2 = 18%

Overall Profit = 14%

Formula Used:

Ratio of Quantities = (Higher Profit % − Mean Profit %) : (Mean Profit % − Lower Profit %)

Calculations:

⇒ Quantity Ratio = (18 − 14) : (14 − 8)

⇒ Ratio = 4 : 6 = 2 : 3

⇒ Total weight parts = 2 + 3 = 5 parts

⇒ 5 units = 1000 kg

⇒ 1 unit = 1000 ÷ 5 = 200 kg

⇒ Quantity sold at 18% profit = 3 units

⇒ Quantity = 3 × 200 = 600 kg

∴ The correct option is B.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

It is used to find the ratio in which two components must be mixed to get a mixture of a desired value: (Quantity 1 / Quantity 2) = (Value 2 − Mean) / (Mean − Value 1).

Profit and Cost Price

Profit % is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Profit = SP − CP.

Mean Value

The mean profit or price always lies between the two individual values (8 < 14 < 18).

questions.question: A solid metallic cube of side 6 \(\sqrt[{3}]{4} \) cm, is melted and recast into a cuboid of length 12 cm and breadth 9 cm. What is the length (in cm) of the longest diagonal of the cuboid?
questions.questionHtml: A solid metallic cube of side 6 \(\sqrt[{3}]{4} \) cm, is melted and recast into a cuboid of length 12 cm and breadth 9 cm. What is the length (in cm) of the longest diagonal of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
Volume of cube = Volume of cuboid

\(( side )^3\) = length × breadth × height

Length of diagonal of cuboid = \(\sqrt{l^2 +b^2+h^2} \) = \(\sqrt{12^2 + 9^2 + 8^2}\) = 17 cm

questions.question: What is the average of first 20 Natural even numbers?
questions.questionHtml: What is the average of first 20 Natural even numbers?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The shortcut formula for the average of the first n even natural numbers is (n + 1).

Given n = 20.

Average = 20 + 1 = 21.

∴ The correct option is C.

Alternate Method

Given: The first 20 even natural numbers are 2, 4, 6, ..., up to the 20th term.

Formula Used: Average of an Arithmetic Progression (AP) = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

⇒ First term (a) = 2

⇒ Last term (l) = 2 × 20 = 40

⇒ Average = (2 + 40) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 42 ÷ 2 = 21

∴ The correct option is C.

Additional Information

Average of first n natural numbers

The average of the first n natural numbers (1, 2, 3, ...) is given by (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Average of first n odd natural numbers

The average of the first n odd natural numbers (1, 3, 5, ...) is exactly equal to n.

Sum of first n even natural numbers

The sum of the first n even natural numbers is calculated using the formula n × (n + 1).

questions.question: The length and the breadth of a rectangular cardboard are 40 cm and 35 cm, respectively. If the biggest possible square is cut out from this cardboard, what is the area of the remaining part of the cardboard?
questions.questionHtml: The length and the breadth of a rectangular cardboard are 40 cm and 35 cm, respectively. If the biggest possible square is cut out from this cardboard, what is the area of the remaining part of the cardboard?

options.html: 275 cm2
425 cm2
325 cm2

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

To cut out the biggest possible square from a rectangle, its side must equal the smaller dimension (breadth).

Side of the square = 35 cm.

The remaining portion is a rectangle with length (40 − 35) = 5 cm and breadth 35 cm.

Remaining Area = 5 × 35 = 175 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 175 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of cardboard (L) = 40 cm

Breadth of cardboard (B) = 35 cm

Formula Used:

Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth

Area of square = Side × Side

Calculations:

⇒ Area of the original cardboard = 40 × 35 = 1400 cm2

⇒ For the biggest possible square, Side (a) = Breadth = 35 cm

⇒ Area of the cut-out square = 35 × 35 = 1225 cm2

⇒ Area of the remaining part = Area of original cardboard − Area of cut-out square

⇒ Area of the remaining part = 1400 − 1225 = 175 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 175 cm2.

Additional Information

Maximum Square from a Rectangle

To cut the largest possible square from a rectangle, the side length of the square must be perfectly equal to the shorter side (breadth) of the given rectangle.

Area of a Rectangle

The area of a rectangle is defined as the product of its length and breadth. Formula: Area = L × B.

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The total distance around the outside boundary of a rectangle. Formula: Perimeter = 2 × (L + B).

questions.question: If the mean of five observations x, x + 2, x + 4, x + 6 and x + 8 is 11, then the mean of the last three observations is:
questions.questionHtml: If the mean of five observations x, x + 2, x + 4, x + 6 and x + 8 is 11, then the mean of the last three observations is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The given observations are in an Arithmetic Progression (A.P.) with a common difference of 2.

For an odd number of terms in an A.P., the mean is exactly the middle term.

The middle term of the 5 observations is (x + 4), so x + 4 = 11 ⇒ x = 7.

The last three observations are (x + 4), (x + 6) and (x + 8).

The mean of these 3 terms is their middle term, which is (x + 6) = 7 + 6 = 13.

∴ The correct answer is 13.

Alternate Method

Given:

Observations: x, x + 2, x + 4, x + 6, x + 8

Mean of these 5 observations = 11

Formula Used:

Mean = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

Calculations:

⇒ Mean = (x + x + 2 + x + 4 + x + 6 + x + 8) ÷ 5

⇒ 11 = (5x + 20) ÷ 5

⇒ 11 = x + 4

⇒ x = 11 − 4

⇒ x = 7

⇒ The last three observations are:

⇒ x + 4 = 7 + 4 = 11

⇒ x + 6 = 7 + 6 = 13

⇒ x + 8 = 7 + 8 = 15

⇒ Mean of last three observations = (11 + 13 + 15) ÷ 3

⇒ Mean = 39 ÷ 3 = 13

∴ The correct answer is 13.

Additional Information

Mean of an Arithmetic Progression (A.P.)

When a set of numbers is in an A.P., their mean is always equal to the exact middle term (if the number of terms is odd) or the average of the two middle terms (if even). It is also equal to (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.

Change in Average with Fixed Addition

If a constant value 'k' is added to or subtracted from every observation in a dataset, the new mean of the observations will also identically increase or decrease by exactly 'k'.

Sum of Consecutive Terms

The sum of 'n' terms in an A.P. can be quickly calculated as n × Average. For instance, the sum of 5 terms with an average of 11 is directly 5 × 11 = 55.

questions.question: A train leaves Hyderabad at 4:00 A.M. and reaches Vijayawada at 8:00 A.M. the same day. Another train leaves Vijayawada at 6:00 A.M. and reaches Hyderabad at 9:30 A.M the same day. At what time do the two trains cross each other?
questions.questionHtml: A train leaves Hyderabad at 4:00 A.M. and reaches Vijayawada at 8:00 A.M. the same day. Another train leaves Vijayawada at 6:00 A.M. and reaches Hyderabad at 9:30 A.M the same day. At what time do the two trains cross each other?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let total distance = LCM of 4 and 3.5 = 28 units. Speeds are 28 ÷ 4 = 7 units/hr and 28 ÷ 3.5 = 8 units/hr.

Train 1 travels from 4:00 A.M. to 6:00 A.M., covering 7 × 2 = 14 units.

Remaining distance = 28 − 14 = 14 units, and Relative speed = 7 + 8 = 15 units/hr.

Time to meet = 14 ÷ 15 hours = 56 minutes after 6:00 A.M., which is 6:56 A.M.

∴ The correct answer is 6:56 A.M.

Alternate Method

Given:

Train 1 timings: 4:00 A.M. to 8:00 A.M. (Time taken = 4 hours)

Train 2 timings: 6:00 A.M. to 9:30 A.M. (Time taken = 3.5 hours = 7/2 hours)

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Time to meet = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Calculations:

⇒ Let the total distance between Hyderabad and Vijayawada be D = 28x km.

⇒ Speed of Train 1 = 28x ÷ 4 = 7x km/h

⇒ Speed of Train 2 = 28x ÷ (7/2) = 8x km/h

⇒ From 4:00 A.M. to 6:00 A.M. (2 hours), Train 1 covers distance = 2 × 7x = 14x km

⇒ Remaining distance at 6:00 A.M. = 28x − 14x = 14x km

⇒ As trains are moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = 7x + 8x = 15x km/h

⇒ Time taken to cross each other = Remaining distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 14x ÷ 15x = 14/15 hours

⇒ Converting into minutes = (14 ÷ 15) × 60 = 56 minutes

⇒ They cross each other 56 minutes after 6:00 A.M. = 6:56 A.M.

∴ The correct answer is 6:56 A.M.

Additional Information

Relative Speed

When two bodies move towards each other (in opposite directions), their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S1 + S2). When moving in the same direction, it is the difference (S1 − S2).

Time of Meeting

To calculate the exact time of meeting, always ensure both moving bodies start at the same reference time. The distance covered by the early starter must be subtracted from the total distance first.

Average Speed

When traveling the same distance at two different speeds S1 and S2, the Average Speed = (2 × S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2).

questions.question: The ratio of income of two persons is 10 ∶ 6 and that of their expenditures is 18 ∶ 10. If they save ₹ 5,200 and ₹ 3,600 respectively, their incomes are :
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of income of two persons is 10 ∶ 6 and that of their expenditures is 18 ∶ 10. If they save ₹ 5,200 and ₹ 3,600 respectively, their incomes are :
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the cross-multiplication method:

Income ratio = 10  ∶  6, Expenditure ratio = 18  ∶  10, Savings = ₹ 5200 and ₹ 3600.

Cross-product difference of ratios = |10 × 10 − 18 × 6| = |100 − 108| = 8 units.

Cross-product difference of expenditures and savings = |18 × 3600 − 10 × 5200| = |64800 − 52000| = 12800.

8 units ≡ 12800 ⇒ 1 unit ≡ 1600.

∴ The correct answer is ₹ 16,000, ₹ 9,600.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Let the incomes of the two persons be 10x and 6x respectively.

⇒ Let their expenditures be 18y and 10y respectively.

⇒ Income − Expenditure = Savings

⇒ Person 1 savings: 10x − 18y = 5200   ... (Equation 1)

⇒ Person 2 savings: 6x − 10y = 3600   ... (Equation 2)

Calculations:

⇒ Multiply Equation 1 by 5: 50x − 90y = 26000

⇒ Multiply Equation 2 by 9: 54x − 90y = 32400

⇒ Subtract the two equations: (54x − 50x) − (90y − 90y) = 32400 − 26000

⇒ 4x = 6400

⇒ x = 1600

⇒ Income of Person 1 = 10x = 10 × 1600 = ₹ 16,000

⇒ Income of Person 2 = 6x = 6 × 1600 = ₹ 9,600

∴ The correct answer is ₹ 16,000, ₹ 9,600.

Additional Information

Income, Expenditure & Savings Relation

The fundamental relation in such problems is always: Income = Expenditure + Savings. This basic equation allows you to construct linear equations from given ratios.

Cross-Multiplication Method

When both the initial quantities and their respective absolute changes (like numerical savings) are known, the cross-product differences between initial ratios and changes yield directly proportional equivalents, bypassing extensive algebra.

questions.question: What is the % profit on the cost price of an article if there is a profit of 20% on the selling price?
questions.questionHtml: What is the % profit on the cost price of an article if there is a profit of 20% on the selling price?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Profit on Selling Price = 20% = 1/5

This means SP = 5 units, Profit = 1 unit.

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Profit = 5 − 1 = 4 units.

Actual Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%.

∴ The correct answer is 25%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Profit calculated on Selling Price (SP) = 20%

Formula Used:

CP = SP − Profit

Actual Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let Selling Price (SP) = 100 units

⇒ Profit = 20% of 100 = 20 units

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = 100 − 20 = 80 units

⇒ Actual Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Actual Profit % = (20 ÷ 80) × 100

⇒ Actual Profit % = 1/4 × 100 = 25%

∴ The correct answer is 25%.

Additional Information

Loss Calculated on Selling Price

If a loss is given as x% on SP, then CP = SP + Loss. The actual loss percentage is (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) unless stated otherwise. Selling Price = MP − (Discount % of MP).

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells at CP but uses false weight, Profit % = (Error ÷ (True Value − Error)) × 100.

questions.question: If the 11-digit number 79x6402087y is divisible by 72, then for smallest value of x, what is the value of (x + 2y)?
questions.questionHtml: If the 11-digit number 79x6402087y is divisible by 72, then for smallest value of x, what is the value of (x + 2y)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a number to be divisible by 72, it must be perfectly divisible by both 8 and 9.

Rule of 8: The last three digits (87y) must be divisible by 8 ⇒ 872 is divisible by 8, so y = 2.

Rule of 9: The sum of digits (45 + x) must be divisible by 9 ⇒ The smallest possible value for x is 0.

Required value = (x + 2y) = 0 + 2 × 2 = 4.

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Alternate Method

Given:

The 11-digit number 79x6402087y is divisible by 72.

Method Used:

If a number is divisible by 72, it must be divisible by its co-prime factors 8 and 9.

Divisibility rule of 8: The number formed by the last three digits must be divisible by 8.

Divisibility rule of 9: The sum of all the digits must be divisible by 9.

Calculations:

⇒ Consider the last 3 digits for divisibility by 8: 87y

⇒ 87y = 800 + 70 + y

⇒ 800 is perfectly divisible by 8, so (70 + y) must also be divisible by 8.

⇒ The closest multiple of 8 to 70 is 72, which gives y = 2.

⇒ So, y = 2. The number now becomes 79x64020872.

⇒ Now, apply the divisibility rule of 9 to the entire number.

⇒ Sum of digits = 7 + 9 + x + 6 + 4 + 0 + 2 + 0 + 8 + 7 + 2

⇒ Sum of digits = 45 + x

⇒ For (45 + x) to be divisible by 9, x can either be 0 or 9 (since 45 is a multiple of 9).

⇒ Since we need the smallest value of x, we take x = 0.

⇒ We need to find the final value of (x + 2y).

⇒ (x + 2y) = 0 + 2 × 2

⇒ (x + 2y) = 4

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is perfectly divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Co-prime Divisibility Theorem

If a number is divisible by two co-prime numbers a and b, it is always divisible by their product (a × b). For example, 72 = 8 × 9.

questions.question: If Sec( 2a - 32°) = Cosec(46 ° - 21a) , then find the value of a?
questions.questionHtml: If Sec( 2a - 32°)  = Cosec(46° - 21a) , then find the value of a?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If Sec(A) = Cosec(B), then A + B = 90°.

⇒ 2a − 32° + 46° − 21a = 90°

⇒ −19a + 14° = 90°

⇒ −19a = 76°

⇒ a = −4°

∴ The correct answer is −4°.

Alternate Method

Given:

Sec(2a − 32°) = Cosec(46° − 21a)

Formula Used:

Cosec(θ) = Sec(90° − θ)

Calculations:

⇒ Sec(2a − 32°) = Sec(90° − (46° − 21a))

⇒ 2a − 32° = 90° − 46° + 21a

⇒ 2a − 32° = 44° + 21a

⇒ 2a − 21a = 44° + 32°

⇒ −19a = 76°

⇒ a = −4°

∴ The correct answer is −4°.

Additional Information

Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their sum is exactly 90°. Trigonometric co-functions of complementary angles are equal: Sin(A) = Cos(B), Tan(A) = Cot(B), and Sec(A) = Cosec(B) when A + B = 90°.

Pythagorean Identities

The fundamental identities are Sin2θ + Cos2θ = 1, 1 + Tan2θ = Sec2θ, and 1 + Cot2θ = Cosec2θ.

Signs in Quadrants

In the 1st quadrant (0° to 90°), all trigonometric ratios are positive. This ASTC rule helps in determining the sign of ratios for larger angles.

questions.questionHtml: A man invested 1/3 of his retirement gratuity at 6% simple interest; 1/4 of his gratuity at 7% and the rest at 8% simple interest. If his annual return on these investments is Rs. 7012.5, find the total amount of gratuity invested by the man.

questions.question: Sapna invests an amount of Rs.80000 to start a business. After 6 months Khyati joined his business with an amount of Rs.30000. If they got a profit of Rs.25500 after one year, then find the share of Khyati in the profit. (rounded off to the nearest rupee)
questions.questionHtml: Sapna invests an amount of Rs.80000 to start a business. After 6 months Khyati joined his business with an amount of Rs.30000. If they got a profit of Rs.25500 after one year, then find the share of Khyati in the profit. (rounded off to the nearest rupee)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Profit ratio = (Capital1 × Time1) : (Capital2 × Time2)

Sapna : Khyati = (80000 × 12) : (30000 × 6) = 16 : 3

Total profit parts = 16 + 3 = 19 parts = 25500

Khyati's share = 3 parts = (25500 ÷ 19) × 3 ≈ 4026.31

∴ The correct answer is ₹4026.

Alternate Method

Given:

Sapna's Investment = ₹80,000

Time period of Sapna = 12 months (since she started the business)

Khyati's Investment = ₹30,000

Time period of Khyati = 12 − 6 = 6 months (since she joined after 6 months)

Total profit = ₹25,500

Formula Used:

Profit Ratio = (Investment1 × Time1) : (Investment2 × Time2)

Calculations:

⇒ Profit Ratio = (80000 × 12) : (30000 × 6)

⇒ Profit Ratio = 960000 : 180000

⇒ Profit Ratio = 96 : 18 = 16 : 3

⇒ Total ratio parts = 16 + 3 = 19

⇒ Khyati's share = (3 ÷ 19) × 25500

⇒ Khyati's share = 76500 ÷ 19 = 4026.315...

⇒ Khyati's share ≈ ₹4026 (rounded off to the nearest rupee)

∴ The correct answer is ₹4026.

Additional Information

Joining Mid-way in Partnership

When a partner joins after a few months, their investment time is calculated from their joining date until the end of the financial year (e.g., 12 − 6 = 6 months).

Compound Ratio in Profits

The profit ratio is the compound ratio of the investment amounts and the respective time periods. Profit = Capital × Time.

Sleeping vs Working Partner

A working partner actively manages the business and usually receives a salary or a fixed percentage of the profit before the remaining profit is distributed. A sleeping partner only invests capital.

questions.question: Ram can do 50% of a work in 24 days, Shyam can do 1/4 th of the work in 36 day. In how many days can they do 1/6 th of the work working together.
questions.questionHtml: Ram can do 50% of a work in 24 days, Shyam can do 1/4<sup>th</sup> of the work in 36 day. In how many days can they do 1/6<sup>th</sup> of the work working together.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ram's 100% work time = 24 × 2 = 48 days; Shyam's 100% work time = 36 × 4 = 144 days.

Total work = LCM of 48 and 144 = 144 units.

Combined efficiency = (144 ÷ 48) + (144 ÷ 144) = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day.

Required work to complete = 1/6 × 144 = 24 units.

Time required = 24 units ÷ 4 units/day = 6 days.

∴ The correct answer is 6 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ram completes 50% (or 1/2) of the work in 24 days.

Shyam completes 1/4th of the work in 36 days.

Formula Used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Total time for Ram to complete 100% work = 24 × 2 = 48 days

⇒ Total time for Shyam to complete 100% work = 36 × 4 = 144 days

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
Ram 48 144 3
Shyam 144 1

⇒ Combined efficiency of Ram and Shyam = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day

⇒ Required work to be done = 1/6th of total work

⇒ Required work = 144 ÷ 6 = 24 units

⇒ Time required = Required work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time required = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 days

∴ The correct answer is 6 days.

Additional Information

Pipes & Cisterns

Works exactly like Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, while outlet pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency. Capacity replaces total work.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in the direct ratio of the total work done by each person. If everyone works for the same number of days, wages are divided based on their daily efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

To solve alternate days problems, calculate the total work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and multiply it to reach just below the total work before finishing the rest sequentially.

questions.question: A pump can fill a tank with water in 3 hours. Because of a leak it took \(3\frac{1}{5}hours\) to fill the tank. The leak can drain all the water in the tank in
questions.questionHtml: A pump can fill a tank with water in 3 hours. Because of a leak it took \(3\frac{1}{5}hours\) to fill the tank. The leak can drain all the water in the tank in
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Capacity = LCM of numerators of 3 and 16/5 = 48 units.

Efficiency of Pump = 48 ÷ 3 = 16 units/hr.

Combined Efficiency of Pump + Leak = 48 ÷ (16/5) = 15 units/hr.

Efficiency of Leak = 16 − 15 = 1 unit/hr (draining).

Time taken by Leak alone = Total Capacity ÷ Leak Efficiency = 48 ÷ 1 = 48 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 48 hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by the pump to fill the tank = 3 hours

Time taken to fill the tank with a leak = 31/5 hours = 16/5 hours

Method Used:

We use the LCM method to find the total capacity of the tank and individual efficiencies.

Pipe/Leak Hours Total Capacity Efficiency
Pump A 3 48 16
Pump A + Leak B 16/5 15

Calculations:

⇒ Efficiency of Leak B = Combined Efficiency − Efficiency of Pump A

⇒ Efficiency of Leak B = 15 − 16 = −1 unit/hour

⇒ The negative sign indicates that Leak B is draining the water at 1 unit/hour.

⇒ Time taken by Leak B to drain the full tank = Total Capacity ÷ Draining Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 48 ÷ 1 = 48 hours

∴ The correct answer is 48 hours.

Additional Information

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank (positive work), while an outlet pipe or leak drains the tank (negative work).

Combined Work Formula

If pipe A fills a tank in x hours and pipe B empties it in y hours (where y > x), the net part filled in 1 hour is (1/x − 1/y).

Total Time to Fill/Empty

Total time = Total Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency. If net efficiency is positive, the tank gets filled. If negative, it gets emptied.

questions.question: Find the value of \(\sqrt{\frac{1-\tan A}{1+\tan A}}\) .
questions.questionHtml: Find the value of \(\sqrt{\frac{1-\tan A}{1+\tan A}}\).
questions.solution:
\(\sqrt{\frac{1-\tan A}{1+\tan A}}\) ⇒ \(\sqrt{\frac{1-\frac{sinA}{cosA}}{1+\frac{sinA}{cosA}}}\) ⇒ \(\sqrt{\frac{\frac{cosA-sinA}{cosA}}{\frac{cosA+sinA}{cosA}}}\)

⇒ \(\sqrt{\frac{cosA-sinA}{cosA+sinA}}\) ⇒ \(\sqrt{\frac{(cosA-sinA)(cosA-sinA)}{(cosA+sinA)(cosA-sinA)}}\) ⇒ \(\sqrt{\frac{(cosA-sinA)^2}{(cosA^2-sinA^2)}}\)

⇒ \(\sqrt{\frac{(cosA^2+sinA^2-2cosAsinA)}{cos2A}}\) ⇒ \(\sqrt{\frac{(1-sin2A)}{cos2A}}\)

questions.question: Which is the largest number that divides 827, 1149 and 1310 to leave the same remainder in each case?
questions.questionHtml: Which is the largest number that divides 827, 1149 and 1310 to leave the same remainder in each case?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The largest number dividing a, b, and c leaving the same remainder = HCF of |a − b|, |b − c|, |c − a|.

⇒ Difference 1 = |1149 − 827| = 322

⇒ Difference 2 = |1310 − 1149| = 161

⇒ Since 322 is a multiple of 161, their HCF is simply 161.

∴ The correct answer is 161.

Alternate Method

Given:

The numbers are 827, 1149, and 1310.

Formula Used:

When the largest number divides x, y, and z to leave the same remainder in each case, the number is given by the HCF of their absolute differences: HCF(|x − y|, |y − z|, |z − x|).

Calculation:

⇒ First difference = |1149 − 827| = 322

⇒ Second difference = |1310 − 1149| = 161

⇒ Third difference = |1310 − 827| = 483

⇒ Now, we need to find the HCF of 322, 161, and 483.

⇒ Factorising the numbers:

⇒ 161 = 161 × 1

⇒ 322 = 161 × 2

⇒ 483 = 161 × 3

⇒ The Highest Common Factor (HCF) is clearly 161.

∴ The correct answer is 161.

Additional Information

Case 1: Different Remainders

To find the largest number that divides x, y, and z leaving remainders a, b, and c respectively, calculate the HCF of (x − a), (y − b), and (z − c).

Case 2: Same Known Remainder

To find the largest number that divides x, y, and z leaving the same given remainder r in each case, calculate the HCF of (x − r), (y − r), and (z − r).

LCM Application

To find the smallest number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves the same remainder r, the formula is LCM(x, y, z) + r.

questions.question: Two objects were sold for ₹9,900 each. One object was sold at a loss of 10% and the other object was sold at a gain of 10%. The net gain or loss in the whole transaction is:
questions.questionHtml: Two objects were sold for ₹9,900 each. One object was sold at a loss of 10% and the other object was sold at a gain of 10%. The net gain or loss in the whole transaction is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two objects are sold at the same SP with x% profit and x% loss, there is always a net loss of x2 ÷ 100%.

Net Loss % = (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 1%.

Total SP = 9900 × 2 = ₹19,800, which is equivalent to 99% of Total CP (100% − 1%).

Loss amount = 1% of CP = (19800 ÷ 99) × 1 = ₹200.

∴ The correct answer is Loss ₹200.

Alternate Method

Given:

SP of first object = ₹9,900, Profit = 10%

SP of second object = ₹9,900, Loss = 10%

Formula Used:

CP = [100 ÷ (100 ± Profit/Loss %)] × SP

Loss = Total CP − Total SP

Calculations:

⇒ CP of first object = [100 ÷ (100 + 10)] × 9900

⇒ CP1 = (100 ÷ 110) × 9900 = ₹9,000

⇒ CP of second object = [100 ÷ (100 − 10)] × 9900

⇒ CP2 = (100 ÷ 90) × 9900 = ₹11,000

⇒ Total CP = 9000 + 11000 = ₹20,000

⇒ Total SP = 9900 + 9900 = ₹19,800

⇒ Net Loss = Total CP − Total SP

⇒ Net Loss = 20000 − 19800 = ₹200

∴ The correct answer is Loss ₹200.

Additional Information

Same Selling Price Condition

When two items are sold at the same price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always an overall loss of (x2 ÷ 100)%.

Cost Price Formula

CP can be directly calculated from SP using: CP = SP × [100 ÷ (100 ± R)], where R is the profit or loss percentage.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: A triangle and a parallelogram are on the same base and between the same parallels. The ratio of the area of triangle and parallelogram is _______.
questions.questionHtml: A triangle and a parallelogram are on the same base and between the same parallels. The ratio of the area of triangle and parallelogram is _______.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By geometric properties, a triangle and a parallelogram on the same base and between the same parallel lines share equal base length and perpendicular height.

Area of triangle = ½ × base × height

Area of parallelogram = base × height

Required Ratio = (½ × base × height) ÷ (base × height) = 1 ÷ 2

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.

Alternate Method

Given:

A triangle and a parallelogram lie on the identical base (b) and strictly between the exact same parallel boundaries.

Formula Used:

Area of a Parallelogram = base × height

Area of a Triangle = ½ × base × height

Calculation:

⇒ Let the shared base of both geometric shapes be 'b'.

⇒ Because they are positioned between the identical pair of parallel lines, the perpendicular height 'h' remains the same for both.

⇒ Area of Parallelogram = b × h

⇒ Area of Triangle = ½ × b × h

⇒ Ratio of Area (Triangle to Parallelogram) = (½ × b × h) ÷ (b × h)

⇒ Ratio = ½ = 1 : 2

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.

Additional Information

Parallelograms on the Same Base

Parallelograms lying on the same base and structurally between the same parallel lines strictly maintain an equal total area relative to each other.

Triangles on the Same Base

Triangles constructed on the exact same base and remaining between the identical parallel lines invariably possess equal area measurements.

Median Area Division

A median traced from any given vertex of a triangle correctly halves the opposing side, thereby bisecting the primary triangle into two individual triangles carrying equal areas.

questions.question: In the given figure, if AB || CD, then find x + y.
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, if AB || CD, then find x + y.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For any zigzag transversal between two parallel lines, the sum of left-pointing angles equals the sum of right-pointing angles.

In the given figure, the transversals form right-pointing angles x and y, and a left-pointing angle of 60°.

Equating the angles pointing in opposite directions directly gives:

x + y = 60°

∴ The correct answer is 60°.

Alternate Method

Given:

Lines AB and CD are parallel (AB || CD).

The interior angle formed at the transversal vertex P is 60°.

The angles formed with the parallel lines are x and y.

Calculations:

⇒ Let us draw an imaginary line XY parallel to AB and CD passing through the point P, such that PX points to the left.

⇒ This line divides the 60° angle at P into two parts: ∠EPX (upper half) and ∠FPX (lower half).

⇒ Since AB || XY, the alternate interior angles formed by the transversal EP are equal:

⇒ ∠EPX = ∠BEP = x

⇒ Since CD || XY, the alternate interior angles formed by the transversal FP are equal:

⇒ ∠FPX = ∠DFP = y

⇒ The total angle on the left side of point P is given as 60°.

⇒ ∴ ∠EPX + ∠FPX = 60°

⇒ Substituting the corresponding values:

⇒ x + y = 60°

∴ The correct answer is 60°.

Additional Information

Parallel Lines & Transversals

When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, alternate interior angles are equal, corresponding angles are equal, and the sum of consecutive interior angles on the same side is exactly 180°.

Zigzag Transversal Rule

If two parallel lines are intersected by one or more zigzag transversals, the sum of all the angles pointing to the left is always equal to the sum of all the angles pointing to the right.

Linear Pair Axiom

If a ray stands on a straight line, the sum of the two adjacent angles formed is 180°. These angles are supplementary and establish a linear pair.

questions.question: Shyam alone can do a piece of work in 40 days working 2 hours a day. Ram alone can do the same work in 60 days working 2 hours a day. How many hours per day do they need to work together to complete the same work in 12 days?
questions.questionHtml: Shyam alone can do a piece of work in 40 days working 2 hours a day. Ram alone can do the same work in 60 days working 2 hours a day. How many hours per day do they need to work together to complete the same work in 12 days?
questions.solution:
Total hours taken by Shyam to complete the work = 40 × 2 = 80 hours

Total hours taken by Ram to complete the work = 60 × 2 = 120 hours

Let total work = LCM(80, 120) = 240 units

The efficiency of Shyam = 240/80 = 3 units, The efficiency of Ram = 240/ 120 = 2 units

They work together for 12 days with the efficiency of (3 + 2) = 5 units

So, they have to work 240/(12 × 5) = 20/5 = 4 hours.

questions.question: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. One should help one's grandparents.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

One should help one's grandparents.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Grandparents should be helped'.

Key Points

  • The above sentence is in passive voice since it emphasizes the action or object of the sentence.
  • The above sentence is a special kind of sentence that is asked in exams and it needs to be learned as it is.
  • For the above sentence, this rule is to be followed:
    • Active voice: One should help one's grandparents.
    • Passive voice: Grandparents should be helped. (better alternative)
                                One's grandparents should be helped.
  • The tense remains the same as the passive voice.
  • Here, the simple present tense is used.   
     

Additional Information

  • ​'One's' is always followed by a noun.
  • If 'one' is used at the beginning of a sentence, then only that should be repeated again. For example:
    • One should help his grandparents. 
    • One should help one's grandparents.
  • Only sentences with the transitive verb can be converted into passive voice and not the ones with an intransitive verb.
  • A transitive verb needs an object to complete its meaning. For example: He answered the questions confidently. (subject + verb + object)
  • The intransitive verb does not have an object. For example: He answered confidently. (subject + verb)
     

Correct sentence: "Grandparents should be helped".

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice:

She said to her brother, "Remember to bring your umbrella with you when you go to school because it looks like it might rain in the afternoon."

options.text: She reminded her brother to remember to bring his umbrella with him when he went to school because it looked like it might rain in the afternoon.

options.html: She reminded her brother to bring your umbrella with you when you go to school because it looks like it might rain in the afternoon.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • Indirect Speech: She reminded her brother to bring his umbrella with him when he went to school because it looked like it might rain in the afternoon.
  • Key Conversions:
    • Reporting verb: "said to" changes to "reminded" (since it's a reminder/instruction).
    • Pronoun changes: "your" becomes "his", "you" becomes "he", "with you" becomes "with him".
    • Tense changes: "go" becomes "went", "looks" becomes "looked".
  • Punctuation and Format:
    • Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
    • The imperative ("Remember to bring") is converted to "reminded...to bring".
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Correct Sentence: She reminded her brother to bring his umbrella with him when he went to school because it looked like it might rain in the afternoon.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "to remember to bring" is redundant; "reminded...to bring" is sufficient.
  • Option 3: Tense is not changed ("goes" and "looks" should be "went" and "looked").
  • Option 4: Pronouns not changed ("your", "you" remain instead of "his", "he").

questions.question: Fill up the blank with the correct option. Nothing but huts __________ there.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill up the blank with the correct option.

Nothing but huts __________ there.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Is". 

 Key Points

  • The phrase 'Nothing but huts' is effectively treated as a singular subject because 'Nothing but' is one of the phrases mentioned in the rule that dictates the verb should agree with the first subject.
  • In this case, 'Nothing' is considered the first subject, which is singular.
  • The verb 'is' agrees with the singular noun 'Nothing,' which is technically the focus of the subject in the sentence, despite referring to multiple items (huts).
  • This rule overrides the typical plural agreement you might expect with the plural noun 'huts' because the construction with 'Nothing but' dictates singular agreement.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 3".

Additional Information

  • Were (Option 1): Would typically be the correct choice for a plural subject ('huts') if not for the specific rule applied here.
  • Are (Option 2): Is the plural present form of 'be' and would align with 'huts' in a different construction without the overriding rule.
  • Have (Option 4): Indicates possession or experience but is irrelevant due to the subject-verb agreement rule highlighted.
